title: Service and maintain irrigation control valves

lessons.title: Servicing isolation, direction control and air valves
lessons.html:
Before any valve service

  • Identify the valve and its function from the system plan.
  • Close upstream (and if needed downstream) isolating valves, switch off the pump or zone, and release pressure through a drain or bleed.
  • Have the correct service kit or spare parts for the make and model.
  • Lay parts out in order on a clean surface as you strip the valve. Take photos if helpful.

Isolation valves

ValveCommon faultsService
Gate valveGland leak at spindle, stiff operation, not sealingTighten or repack the gland; clean and grease spindle threads; replace wedge or seat if worn
Ball valveLeaks at stem, handle loose, seals wornReplace stem O-rings and seat seals with kit; replace valve if ball is scored
Butterfly valveLiner worn, disc not sealingReplace liner or seat; check disc and shaft

Operate isolation valves fully open and closed periodically so they do not seize.

Direction control valves

  • Non-return (check) valves: faults include stuck open (water runs back, pumps lose prime), stuck closed (no flow), slamming (water hammer). Strip, clean debris, replace the flap, spring or seal, and check the seat for damage.
  • Foot valves: clean the strainer, check the flap or poppet seals so the pump stays primed.
  • Three-way valves: on filter backwash, check the diaphragm or seal and command tubes.

Air release valves

Faults: leaking water continuously (seal dirty or worn, float damaged), not releasing air (orifice blocked, float stuck). Strip, clean the float and orifice, replace seals, and check the float moves freely. Ensure the isolating valve below the air valve is open after service.

lessons.title: Hydraulic and solenoid valve malfunctions
lessons.html:
How diaphragm valves work

Most irrigation control valves are diaphragm valves. Water from upstream enters the chamber above the diaphragm through a small bleed port. Because the area on top is larger, the diaphragm is held closed. To open the valve, the water above is vented, either by a hydraulic command (hydraulic valve) or by a solenoid opening a pilot port (solenoid valve). Upstream pressure then lifts the diaphragm.

Hydraulic valve malfunctions

MalfunctionPossible causeRemedy
Does not openCommand tube blocked or kinked; controller or command valve not venting; diaphragm stuckCheck and flush command tubes; check controller; strip and clean
Does not closeLeaking command tube; blocked bleed port; torn diaphragm; debris on seatRepair tube; clean port; replace diaphragm; clean seat
Slow closingPartly blocked port or filter on the command circuitClean
Chatter or noiseLow flow for valve size, air in chamberAdjust flow control; bleed air

Solenoid valve malfunctions

MalfunctionPossible causeRemedy
Does not open electrically but opens with manual bleedElectrical fault: no voltage, broken wire, failed solenoid coilMeasure voltage at the valve; measure coil resistance; repair wire or replace solenoid
Does not open at allFlow control closed; upstream isolating valve closed; diaphragm stuckOpen flow control and isolation; clean valve
Does not closeDebris under diaphragm, blocked bleed port, plunger stuck, manual bleed open, solenoid looseClean; replace plunger or diaphragm; close bleed; tighten solenoid by hand
WeepingWorn seat, small debris, diaphragm damageClean or replace parts

Stripping a solenoid valve

  1. Isolate and depressurise.
  2. Turn the solenoid anticlockwise to remove it, keeping the plunger and spring together.
  3. Undo the bonnet screws and lift off the bonnet; remove the spring and diaphragm.
  4. Clean the bleed port with a fine wire, wash the diaphragm and seat, inspect for tears or warping.
  5. Replace damaged parts with the manufacturer's kit, reassemble with the diaphragm seated correctly, tighten screws evenly.

lessons.title: Servicing pressure control valves and documentation
lessons.html:
Pressure control valves

Pressure reducing, sustaining and relief valves are usually pilot-operated: a small pilot valve senses pressure and controls the main valve.

Common malfunctions

SymptomPossible cause
Downstream pressure too high (PRV)Pilot blocked, main diaphragm torn, debris on seat, pilot set wrong
Downstream pressure too lowPilot filter blocked, main valve partly stuck, setting too low
Pressure hunting (fluctuating)Air in control chamber, speed control needle mis-set, valve oversized for the flow
Relief valve leaking continuouslySeat damage, debris, setting too close to working pressure

Servicing steps

  1. Record the current pilot setting and pressures before work.
  2. Isolate and depressurise.
  3. Clean the pilot filter or strainer; flush control tubing.
  4. Strip the pilot: clean, replace diaphragm and seals from the kit.
  5. Strip the main valve: replace diaphragm or seals, clean the seat.
  6. Reassemble; restore pressure slowly while bleeding air from the control chamber.
  7. Set the pilot to the required pressure using a calibrated gauge downstream (PRV) or upstream (sustaining), adjusting in small steps.
  8. Check stable operation at low and high flow.

Never set a relief valve above the pressure rating of the pipes and components it protects.

Testing after any valve service

  • Valve opens and closes correctly on command
  • No leaks at body, bonnet, fittings
  • Correct pressure and flow downstream
  • Isolation valves restored to their normal positions

Documentation

  • Valve location, type, make, model and size
  • Fault found and cause
  • Parts replaced and kit numbers
  • Settings before and after
  • Date and technician
  • Recommendations, such as installing a filter upstream if debris keeps causing faults

Key points

  • Isolate and depressurise before stripping any valve.
  • Most control valves are diaphragm valves held closed by upstream pressure on top.
  • If a solenoid valve opens on manual bleed but not electrically, the fault is electrical.
  • Debris, blocked bleed ports and torn diaphragms cause most failures to close.
  • Record settings, set pilots with a calibrated gauge and document all work.

quiz.question: What should you do before stripping any irrigation valve?

options.text: Isolate it and release the pressure

quiz.question: A non-return valve stuck open at a pump will cause what?

options.text: Water running back and the pump losing prime

quiz.question: A solenoid valve opens with the manual bleed but not from the controller. Where is the fault?

options.text: Electrical: voltage, wiring or solenoid coil
